gaps.sentence: ___ heavy demand, tickets are limited to four per person.
gaps.explanation: 'Owing to + noun' introduces the cause in announcements and notices.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets cost more, but they sold out in minutes.
gaps.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', auxiliary inversion applies: Not only did the tickets cost more.

gaps.sentence: The flat is spacious and well located; ___, the rent is surprisingly low.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds another supporting point in the same direction.

gaps.sentence: She took an evening job ___ fund her law degree.
gaps.explanation: 'In order to' + bare infinitive expresses purpose after a noun phrase subject.

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: ___ feeling nervous, she delivered a flawless presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + -ing expresses concession with a non-finite form.

gaps.sentence: The lecture was dull; ___, the students stayed awake out of politeness.
___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.
